items.text: Structures: groups, rings, modules, comodules, $G$-sets, principal homogeneous spaces — expressed by direct limits, inverse limits and arrows between them.
Exactness property of a category: e.g. filtering direct limits commute with finite inverse limits.
Every type of algebraic structure has a classifying topos (universal representative); axioms added $\leftrightarrow$ subtopoi.

$D=(D',D'')$: sets of diagrams. $\mathbf{Cat}_D$: categories in which inverse limits of type $D'$ and direct limits of type $D''$ exist; functors commuting with these limits; 2-morphisms = morphisms of functors.
Given by $(I,\Sigma)$: $I\in\mathbf{Cat}_D$, $\Sigma\subset\operatorname{Fl}(I)$ a set of arrows.
Conjunction of $(I_\lambda,\Sigma_\lambda)_\lambda$: one property $(I,\Sigma)$, $I$ the 2-sum of the $I_\lambda$.
$J$ a category. Is there $\widehat J$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$ and $J\to\widehat J$ universal?
True if $D'$ or $D''$ is small (adjoin the limits of type $D'$, $D''$).

$X\xrightarrow{f}S\xleftarrow{g}Y$. Naive fibre product: objects $(x,y)$ with $f(x)=g(y)$, arrows likewise ($\operatorname{Ob}X\times_{\operatorname{Ob}S}\operatorname{Ob}Y$, $\operatorname{Fl}X\times_{\operatorname{Fl}S}\operatorname{Fl}Y$).
Not invariant under equivalence: can be empty for an equivalent diagram.
(x,y,\alpha)\to(x',y',\alpha'):\ (u\colon x\to x',\ v\colon y\to y')\ \text{with}\ \alpha'\circ f(u)=g(v)\circ\alpha
Definition of the 2-fibre product $P$ in any 2-category: unique up to equivalence, which is unique up to unique isomorphism.
